text:
The city at night unfolds like a vast, luminous tapestry, where each skyscraper stands as a towering pillar of wax, burning with the steady, unwavering flame of human ambition. Just as a candle relies on its solid core to sustain its glow, the urban landscape draws its vitality from the dense, structured materials of steel and glass that form its skeleton. These structures are not merely buildings but the very wicks of the metropolis, drawing up the energy of the day to cast a vibrant fluorescence against the deep indigo sky. In this nocturnal masterpiece, the city does not just shine; it consumes and transforms, much like a candle melting itself to provide light, turning the raw, hard materials of construction into a soft, inviting radiance that wakes the world while the rest of the earth sleeps.

The primary material of a candle is wax.
